column1: # Example sample sheet for EPICC.
# Copy to your analysis folder, edit, and pass to epicc:
#   epicc run --samples my_samples.tsv ...
# Lines starting with '#' are skipped, so you can park samples without
# deleting their rows.
# Columns (tab-separated, in this order). There is no Sample_ID column: each
# sample's name is derived from its other columns as
#   {level values}_{IP_target}_{Replicate_ID}   ChIP          WT_leaf_H3K9me2_rep1
#   {level values}_CR_{IP_target}_{Rep}         CUT_RUN (CT_ for CUT_TAG)
#   {level values}_{assay}_{Replicate_ID}       other assays  WT_leaf_RNA_rep1
# where {assay} is ATAC, RNA, RAMPAGE, sRNA, WGBS, WGBS_nd, PBAT, EMseq or dmC.
# Two rows must not derive the same name: distinct libraries differ in
# Replicate_ID (or IP_target); several runs of one library go in one row,
# their Read_files joined with '+'. Level values, IP_target and Replicate_ID
# become part of file names, so no whitespace, '/', '__' or leading/trailing '_'.
#   Assay        ChIP | CUT_RUN | CUT_TAG | ATAC | RNAseq | RAMPAGE |
#                sRNA | WGBS | WGBS_nd | PBAT | EMseq | dmC
#   Genome       Reference genome name (must match `genomes:` key in the
#                options YAML). Comma-separate to map the same reads to
#                several references (e.g. ColCEN,TAIR10): reads are downloaded
#                and trimmed once, then aligned to each, and post-alignment
#                files are tagged with the genome. Must not contain '__'.
#   Levels       Comma-separated factor:level pairs (genotype:WT,tissue:leaf).
#                All rows in the sheet must use the same factor keys.
#                No '=' in factor names or levels.
#   Replicate_ID Replicate label (rep1, rep2, repA, ...).
#   Read_files   SRA/ENA/DDBJ accession (SRR12345), local FASTQ/BAM path,
#                HTTP(S) URL, public s3:// URI, or '+'-separated list to merge
#                multiple inputs.
#                For PE FASTQs at explicit paths: comma-separate R1,R2.
#   Read_layout  SE or PE.
#   IP_target    Required for ChIP / CUT_RUN / CUT_TAG (H3K9me2, Input, WCE,
#                etc.). Blank for other assays.
#   Control      Derived name of the matching control (Input/WCE for ChIP),
#                e.g. Col0_WT_Input_rep1.
#                Leave blank on a control row, unless that control is also
#                analysed against its own control (e.g. H3 normalized to Input);
#                a chain is at most two deep.
#   Peak_type    broad | narrow — the peak-calling type, a separate parameter
#                from the assay. Required on ChIP / CUT_RUN / CUT_TAG rows with a
#                Control, optional on a control-only row (broad
#                for histone domains like H3K9me2/H3K27me3; narrow for TFs and
#                sharp marks like H3K4me3/H3K27ac). Blank for all other assays.
#                Applies to only three assays, so it sits near the end.
#   Comments     Optional free text for your own notes (batch, library prep,
#                sequencing run, anything). Completely ignored by the pipeline —
#                it never affects analysis names or outputs. Last column.
# See dev/docs/sample-sheet-spec.md for the full per-field specification
# and tools/epicc-builder.html for an interactive editor.
